did_you_know.text: Did you know? The Ziphites went to Saul and told him that David was hiding at the hill of Hakilah, overlooking Jeshimon. This is the second time in the book of Samuel that the Ziphites reveal David’s location to Saul.
Did you know? Saul went into the wilderness of Ziph with three thousand men chosen from Israel to search for David.
Did you know? David did not rely only on rumors: he sent out spies, and they confirmed that Saul had indeed arrived at the camp.
Did you know? David chose Abishai son of Zeruiah to go with him to Saul’s camp. Abishai is described here as the brother of Joab, who would later become David’s army commander.
Did you know? Abishai saw Saul’s sleep as an opportunity God had given David to defeat his enemy, but David refused to kill Saul.
Did you know? David calls Saul “the Lord’s anointed” and insists that he must not harm the king. In this way, he shows his loyalty to Saul’s sacred position, even while Saul is pursuing him.
Did you know? David and Abishai managed to take Saul’s spear and water jug without anyone noticing, because a deep sleep from the Lord had fallen over the entire camp.
Did you know? David uses the spear and water jug as proof that Abner, Saul’s army commander, had failed to guard the sleeping king properly.
Did you know? David describes his persecution as a situation that drives him away from the Lord’s inheritance, and he compares himself to a small flea being hunted in the mountains.

Did you know? Saul openly admits, “I have sinned” and “I have acted foolishly and made a mistake.” Despite his confession and his blessing of David, at the end of the chapter David and Saul do not return to living together: David goes his way, and Saul returns to his place.
